title: What Causes Complex Trauma?
metaDescription: Understand the causes of complex trauma and take the first steps toward healing with our Trauma Quiz and trauma-informed coaching support.

author.name: Jenna Barbosa
author.bio: Jenna Barbosa, MA, is a Certified Biblical Counselor and Emotional Freedom Life Coach. She holds certifications and degrees from the AACC's Light University, Lindenwood University, and Missouri Baptist University. She is the head coach at [jennarhae.com](/), offering trauma recovery and faith-based counseling.

sections.text: A good way to understand complex trauma is to recognize that it’s caused by **repeated or prolonged exposure** to what we can think of as highly stressful, overwhelming, or harmful experiences — the kind that affect us emotionally, physically, mentally, or even relationally.
In this blog post, we’re going to take a closer look at **what causes complex trauma** — so you can be empowered to understand what you or a loved one may be going through.
Here’s what you’ll learn:

items: What kinds of experiences often lead to complex trauma
How powerlessness plays a central role in trauma
Why early attachment wounds can shape emotional safety
How relationships and environments can keep trauma patterns alive

sections.text: So, what actually happens when trauma develops?
Let’s start with one of the biggest indicators of all: **powerlessness**.
Powerlessness: The Core of Trauma
Whenever a person feels **trapped or powerless**, that’s a major dynamic of trauma. In fact, **powerlessness really is the currency of trauma**.

If we truly understand trauma at its core, we see that it carries a deep sense of fear — the belief that there’s no power to overcome what’s happening. That sense of being unable to escape, to change, or to be heard, becomes one of the most defining elements of complex trauma.
So, where does this begin for most people?
Let’s talk about **childhood experiences**.
Childhood Experiences and Complex Trauma
Many people who struggle with complex trauma trace it back to **childhood experiences**. These might include ongoing abuse — whether **physical, emotional, sexual, or verbal**.
But trauma doesn’t always come from direct harm.
Sometimes it comes from **what’s missing**.
The Role of Neglect and Chaos

When a child grows up in a home that’s **chaotic, unsafe, or unpredictable**, it can have the same effect. This might happen when there’s substance abuse, mental illness in caregivers, or just an overall lack of consistent care and safety.

Those kinds of environments create chronic stress in the developing emotional system. Over time, that stress becomes overwhelming — especially for a child who doesn’t yet have the tools to process it.
And that’s where complex trauma often begins to take root.
Now let’s look at how **attachment wounds** deepen that impact:
Attachment Wounds and Emotional Safety
A lot of attachment wounds happen when the basic needs for **safety, love, affirmation, encouragement, and connection** are not met — or not met consistently enough to help a child feel secure.

When a child learns that their needs won’t be reliably met, they also learn that the world isn’t safe. That sense of uncertainty in relationships often carries into adulthood — shaping how they trust, connect, and respond to others.
But attachment wounds aren’t the only cause.
There’s another powerful layer we need to consider: what happens in *relationships marked by control* or abuse.
Powerlessness in Relationships
That same sense of being trapped or powerless can also develop later in life — especially within **abusive or controlling relationships**.
This can happen in families, romantic relationships, workplaces, or even religious settings.
Think of experiences like **harassment, bullying, gaslighting, or manipulation** over long periods of time.
When someone is exposed to those patterns again and again, they begin to feel the same trapped powerlessness they may have felt as a child.
And over time, that’s what shapes the emotional imprint of complex trauma.
So, if it’s not just about childhood and not just about relationships — what else plays a role?
Take a look:
Unsafe Environments and Ongoing Stress
Complex trauma can also come from **repeated exposure to unsafe or violent environments**.
That might look like growing up or living in a neighborhood with chronic violence, being in or near a **war zone**, or even living with someone who carries trauma from such experiences.
When a loved one brings that trauma home — maybe a family member returning from war or an environment marked by chronic conflict — it can create a constant sense of tension in the relationship.
That ongoing exposure to fear or instability keeps the nervous system locked in survival mode.
But there’s one more piece that often lies underneath it all.
The Deep Wound of Betrayal
At the heart of many complex trauma stories lies **betrayal** — the breaking of trust by someone who was supposed to provide safety.

When parents fail to protect or nurture their children, it can leave behind a lasting sense of **betrayal and abandonment**. The child may grow up believing that safety doesn’t exist, or that people who claim to love them can’t be trusted.
That same pattern can show up later in life — through partners, spiritual leaders, or authority figures who misuse trust and power.
The combination of **powerlessness and betrayal** becomes a defining feature of complex trauma.
And that brings us to the bigger picture.
Self-Assessment: Recognizing the Signs
Sometimes it’s hard to tell whether what you’ve been through qualifies as trauma — especially when it’s been part of your life for a long time.
If you’re wondering how your past may be affecting you today, take a few minutes to complete our [**Trauma Quiz**](/trauma-recovery-coaching/#trauma-quiz).
It’s a gentle, insight-driven self-assessment designed to help you better understand the emotional and physical patterns that might be connected to complex trauma.
Awareness is often the first step toward healing — and this quiz can help you take that step with clarity and compassion.
Here are some final thoughts:
Bringing It All Together

Complex trauma usually begins **early in life**, but it doesn’t stop there. It can continue to build through later experiences — through relationships, environments, and circumstances that repeat the same patterns of fear and helplessness.
At its core, complex trauma develops through **prolonged exposure to overwhelming stress**, combined with a deep sense of **powerlessness and betrayal**.
Understanding these roots doesn’t just explain what happened — it opens the door to healing.
Because once we see where trauma comes from, we can begin to reclaim what it took away: our safety, our trust, and our sense of power.
If this resonates with you, know that you don’t have to navigate it alone.
Working with a [trauma coach](/trauma-recovery-coaching/) can help you make sense of your story, rebuild trust with yourself, and begin the process of true recovery from complex trauma.
